purpose: Drives run through root execution, descendant drain, tree stop and output settlement.
behavior: Forces stdin closed unless input exists; feed ignores Closed when the child exits or stops reading early.
A root exit opens one grace window; stopping descendants gets only remaining grace, then output is awaited for a bounded drain even if the supervisor fails.

Absolute deadline starts before spawn; finishing at/after it returns Timeout despite late timer delivery. Aborted rejects with partial result; output/input break overrides Normal/Timeout, and failed stop returns Io with result only when root status is known.
contracts: run never reports completion before its stop attempt and output settle; nonzero ordinary exit remains a successful Result.
dependencies: process/deadline enforces actual timeout; io/collect supplies ordered loss/limit results.
failures_or_limits: Source cannot establish completion under all OS failures; Unstopped explicitly preserves inability to confirm cleanup.

purpose: Runs the QA-E mixed-command lifecycle stress workload through public APIs.
behavior: Defines 200 commands in batches of 20 across 14 deterministic kinds: success, nonzero exit, lines, stdin, pipe holders, resisting trees, timeout/cancel, race, drop, pre-cancel and output limit.

Each command must settle within 5 s; the shared log must satisfy pids.len() >= started, an aggregate lower bound on complete PID entries. That count does not identify every expected root individually; assert_dead_logged subsequently checks the PIDs actually recorded.
Cancellation race allows only ordinary success or Aborted with result, while pre-cancel must have no result.
contracts: K1/K2 in comments are intended test acceptance conditions, not observed measurements here.
dependencies: omni-fixture logs actual process starts; process/tests helpers check OS liveness.
failures_or_limits: Arbitrary timings use a fixed LCG spread, not random exhaustive scheduling.

purpose: Regresses large Spawn environment transport with attached pipe descriptors.
behavior: Sets OMNI_BIG to 64 KiB of x; the source comment compares that size with an 8 KiB socket buffer and Linux's 128 KiB limit for one environment string. This test does not measure/configure socket capacity or establish that EMSGSIZE or its fallback branch occurred.

Configures a 30 s command timeout and requires successful exit, text.starts_with("OMNI_BIG=\"xxx"), and text.trim_end().len() == big.len() + 11; the assertions do not compare the complete returned value or validate full framing.
contracts: Targets macOS EMSGSIZE fallback without suppressing descriptor transfer.
dependencies: client/unix::send handles first-byte SCM_RIGHTS retry; omni-fixture getenv emits the value.
failures_or_limits: One value size is tested; this is not a maximum environment-size guarantee.

purpose: Exercises deadline behavior beyond root exit and Rust future lifetime guarantees.
behavior: Cancellation after root exit must kill a pipe holder while preserving root code; Unix pipe-free lingering members still time out.
Inspects Arc strong/weak counts to require watcher release after natural end, stop, drop or disappearing descendants.
Single-thread caller runtime must make progress alongside run; resisting output holders receive one grace only; 200 zero-timeout runs must all report Timeout; dropping a pending run kills its tree.
contracts: Liveness comes from OS checks and all waits have failure bounds; Send is checked for run futures.
dependencies: process/deadline, run and child Drop are exercised with real fixture/supervisor binaries.
failures_or_limits: Reference counts check current implementation lifecycle; tests have not executed in this session.

purpose: Pins pure Exit conversion, OS signal naming and stop-grace rounding.
behavior: Table covers normal/nonzero/full-u32 exit codes, signal status and Killed/Timeout/Aborted precedence, preserving native code/signal.
success is true only for ordinary Exit with code zero; signal-name cases distinguish Linux and BSD/macOS numbering plus numeric fallback.
Grace rounds any positive fractional millisecond upward and rejects values beyond u32 milliseconds.
contracts: These are pure semantic assertions, independent of a running supervisor.
dependencies: process/exit.rs and process/life::grace are the implementation under test.
failures_or_limits: MemoryExceeded is supported by implementation but absent from this older precedence table.

purpose: Tests supervisor cleanup when the Rust host ends through several distinct paths.
behavior: Role spawns and intentionally forgets a resisting three-process tree so host destructors cannot provide cleanup.
Parent verifies all PIDs alive, releases a stdin gate, then checks exact host exit status for return, process::exit, libtest panic, hard kill, Unix group SIGINT and SIGTERM.
All recorded tree members must die within 300 ms grace plus reaction allowance; Role Drop kills/reaps a failed helper.
contracts: The host installs no custom signal handler in these roles.
dependencies: Real supervisor and omni-fixture provide host-death behavior; process/tests OS observers check liveness.
failures_or_limits: Panic is observed through a libtest subprocess exiting 101, not an arbitrary application panic runtime.

purpose: Tests run partial-result preservation and watcher release after Unix supervisor loss.
behavior: Isolated run lets an escaped output holder remain after root exit, confirms root report through a later probe, then kills its own supervisor.
run must return Io within the drain/window allowance with known root code/reason and ROOT output preserved.
A separate lingering role kills supervisor and requires its weak watcher reference to disappear without firing cancellation.
contracts: Escaped holder and pipe-free member are explicitly killed by the test because Unix supervisor death can leave trees unprotected.
dependencies: host.rs provides isolated role harness; process/run and deadline handle supervisor loss.
failures_or_limits: This source exposes a Unix containment limit and cleans it up; it does not prove supervisor crash kills descendants.

purpose: Checks memory cap semantics through real public run/spawn operations.
behavior: A 256 MiB root against 64 MiB cap must return MemoryExceeded, not success.
A descendant-only 256 MiB allocation must give root MemoryExceeded and eventually empty inventory.
An 8 MiB workload under a 1 GiB cap must survive at least one second and exit normally.
contracts: Root wait can precede completion of tree stop, so descendant case polls inventory afterward.
dependencies: process/memory.rs uses sysinfo sampling; omni-fixture allocates controlled memory.
failures_or_limits: Does not cover short spikes, failed inventories, escaped descendants or exact RSS thresholds. Tests remain NOT_RUN.

purpose: Supplies real-supervisor fixture startup, bounded waits and OS liveness observers for process tests.
behavior: Requires workspace-built binaries, stages supervisor atomically beside test executable when no override exists, and warms binaries to exclude initial macOS validation delay.
Started owns Life and unread marker-sized stdio, kills on drop and tracks PID logs; caller futures run on a separate bounded runtime.
Linux /proc and macOS ps reject observation failures; Windows tasklist identifies fixture names and optional command-line log matching mitigates fast PID reuse.
contracts: Liveness must be checked externally rather than trusting library process inventory.
dependencies: omni-fixture and hugr-omni-supervisor binaries are required before tests.
failures_or_limits: Windows command_line failures return empty text, which may remove an otherwise live PID from the log-filtered set; source does not turn that failure into explicit unknown.

purpose: Verifies Child Drop kills resisting trees even after caller-runtime teardown.
behavior: Uses fixture PID markers to establish a root plus two resistant descendants.
Drops PipeChild on a separate thread within one second and requires all PIDs dead within another second.
Repeats after destroying the caller Tokio runtime, demonstrating intended independence of library background work.
contracts: Timeout or panic of Drop fails through the completion channel.
dependencies: Child Drop and dedicated client runtime are exercised with real supervisor and OS checks.
failures_or_limits: This asserts a bounded observed outcome when run; no runtime evidence was produced here.

purpose: Checks tree inventory, stop deadlines and Exit preservation against OS-observed fixture trees.
behavior: Four-level cooperative tree must list names/parents, stop inside one fifth of grace, become empty and return identical Exit on repeated stop.
After root exits code 5, descendants stay live/listed without the root; later cleanup keeps the same root result.
Cooperative termination with code zero is Killed; resisting trees wait until grace then force; detached kill acts immediately; raw exit/signal statuses remain unchanged.
contracts: Inventory parent links include only listed parents and success excludes library-caused code zero.
dependencies: process::Life mediates real supervisor; helpers use external OS liveness.
failures_or_limits: Timing allowances are test bounds rather than published latency measurements.

purpose: Documents that host PTY behavior is composed from existing client, process and I/O layers.
behavior: Contains only the cfg(test) module declaration; runtime terminal wiring resides in process::spawn_pty.
Names io pumps/stdin and client Go/Resize as terminal responsibilities, with reader-before-Go ordering.
contracts: No separate host PTY transport or process creator is introduced here.
dependencies: process/child.rs orchestrates startup; io/queue/reader.rs and client::Tree implement the cited parts.
failures_or_limits: Architecture comment is not an additional implementation or execution result.

purpose: Regresses immediate-exit Unix terminal output and synchronous held-root exec failures.
behavior: Repeats a print-and-exit PTY launch 300 times and compares exact RUN-i CRLF output with no missing runs.
An executable-mode file containing nonprogram text must fail spawn_pty itself with NotExecutable, matching pipe spawn.
Requires real built binaries and bounded caller futures; stages/warms the supervisor once.
contracts: Unix-only because ConPTY renders extra control sequences; Windows has separate coverage.
dependencies: process spawn_pty reader-before-Go ordering and Unix supervisor exec handshake are exercised.
failures_or_limits: The 300-run claim is a test loop/acceptance threshold, not an observed success count in this analysis.
